sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849

items.exp: 1° adrenal insufficiency = Addison's disease; 2° (m/c) follows abrupt steroid withdrawal, pituitary or hypothalamic dysfunction. (Book p849)

items.q: The most common cause of SECONDARY adrenal insufficiency is:
items.exp: 2° adrenal insufficiency (m/c overall pattern): abrupt steroid withdrawal is m/c, then pituitary and hypothalamic dysfunction. (Book p849)

items.q: The most common cause of Addison's overall is:
items.exp: Autoimmune is m/c overall: polyglandular autoimmune syndrome (PGA)/(APS) type 1 & 2 with anti 21-OH hydroxylase antibody (+), or isolated autoimmune adrenalitis. (Book p849)

items.q: Match the inherited cause — 1) Aladin gene mutation  2) X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy  3) T-pit mutation … A) ↑ very long chain fatty acid  B) Affects only corticotrophs  C) 3A/4A syndrome (alacrimia, achalasia cardia, Addison's, ANS)
items.exp: Aladin mutation → 3A/4A syndrome (alacrimia, achalasia cardia, Addison's, 4th A = ANS); X-ALD → ↑ VLCFA; T-pit affects only corticotrophs. (Book p849)

items.q: The m/c infective cause of Addison's in India is:
items.exp: TB is m/c in India; meningococcaemia (children) causes Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome. (Book p849)

items.q: Meningococcaemia in children causing adrenal haemorrhage is called:
The adrenal gland size in Addison's may be:
items.exp: Size in Addison's: enlarged, normal, atrophic, or asymmetrical. (Book p849)

items.q: Which group of features belongs to glucocorticoid (GC) deficiency?
opts: Asthenia, anorexia, weight loss, hypoglycaemia, eosinophilia
items.exp: GC ↓↓↓: asthenia, anorexia, weakness, weight loss, fatigue, joint pain, hypoglycaemia + hypotension, postural hypotension, euvolemic hyponatremia, eosinophilia. (Book p849)

items.q: Hyperkalaemia, acidosis, hypovolemic hyponatremia, salt craving and ↑BUN/creatinine (pre-renal) reflect deficiency of:
items.exp: MC ↓↓↓: hyperkalaemia, acidosis, hypovolemic hyponatremia, salt cravings, ↑BUN & creatinine (d/t pre-renal failure). (Book p849)

items.q: Dry atrophic skin, loss of axillary/pubic hair and loss of libido reflect loss of:
items.exp: SS ↓↓↓: dry atrophic skin, loss of axillary & pubic hair, loss of libido. (Book p849)

items.q: Hyperpigmentation in Addison's (from ↑ACTH) is seen in about:
items.exp: ACTH ↑↑ → hyperpigmentation (90%) in sun-exposed areas and oral mucosa. (Book p849)

items.q: The additional features listed are normocytic normochromic anemia and hypercalcaemia with:
opts: Auricular calcification (calcification absent in the adrenal gland)
items.exp: Additional: normocytic normochromic anemia; hypercalcaemia → auricular calcification, while calcification is absent in the adrenal gland. (Book p849)
